item.title: Mathematics
item.description:
Maths lessons focus on clear understanding, careful working, and confidence with unfamiliar questions. Students learn why a method works, how to choose a strategy, and how to show their thinking clearly.

Best For

  • Students who need stronger foundations in number, fractions, algebra, or geometry.
  • Students who understand ideas in class but lose marks through weak working or exam habits.
  • Students ready for extension, enrichment, or more challenging problem solving.

Focus Areas

  • Number sense, calculation accuracy, fractions, decimals, percentages, and ratio.
  • Algebra, equations, graphs, geometry, measurement, statistics, and probability.
  • Word problems, logical reasoning, checking strategies, and assessment preparation.

Class Style

Lessons usually combine short explanations, guided examples, independent practice, and review of common mistakes. Each student has targeted tasks, so students in the same small group may still work on different priorities.

item.title: Science
item.description:
Science lessons help students connect school topics with real observations, diagrams, data, and everyday examples. The aim is to move beyond memorising facts and build the ability to explain what is happening and why.

Best For

  • Students who find science vocabulary or explanations difficult.
  • Students who need help with investigations, variables, graphs, and evidence.
  • Students preparing for school assessments in physics, chemistry, biology, or earth science topics.

Focus Areas

  • Scientific investigation, fair testing, variables, data, and graph interpretation.
  • Forces, energy, electricity, waves, matter, chemical change, cells, ecosystems, earth, and space.
  • Using evidence to write clearer scientific explanations.

Class Style

Lessons use questions, models, diagrams, simple investigations, and exam-style explanation practice. Students are encouraged to describe, compare, predict, and justify their ideas in their own words.
